This vignette walks through a complete post-census workflow for one permanent
forest plot, using only data shipped with the package. Every step runs
offline and writes to a temporary directory.

The workflow answers four questions a field team faces after a census:

1. Which trees were vouchered, and where do their photographs go?
2. Where are the collected and uncollected trees in the plot?
3. How complete is the collection, per subplot and per species?
4. How do the vouchers become herbarium labels?

```{r setup}
library(forplotR)

out <- file.path(tempdir(), "forplotR_vignette")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## The example plot

`RUS01` is a ForestPlots.net standard field sheet of a 1-ha plot (100
subplots of 10 x 10 m) in the Reserva Biologica Augusto Ruschi, an Atlantic
Forest reserve in Espirito Santo, Brazil. As in the original sheet, the column
names carry the plot metadata and the first row holds the field headers:

```{r data}
dim(RUS01)
names(RUS01)[1:3]
unlist(RUS01[1, c(1, 3, 5:8, 23, 25)])
```

All `forplot_*()` functions read the Excel file exactly as it is exported
from ForestPlots.net, so we first write the data to disk:

```{r write}
fp <- file.path(out, "RUS01.xlsx")
openxlsx::write.xlsx(RUS01, fp)
```

## 1. Organize voucher image folders

`forplot_vouchers()` creates one folder per collected voucher, nested by
family and species. Photographs dropped in those folders are found later by
`forplot_map()`. When the identification of a voucher changes in a later
version of the sheet, rerunning the function moves its images to the new
folder.

```{r vouchers}
img_dir <- file.path(out, "voucher_imgs")
forplot_vouchers(fp, output_dir = img_dir, verbose = FALSE)

families <- list.dirs(img_dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = FALSE)
length(families)
head(families)
head(list.dirs(file.path(img_dir, families[1]), full.names = FALSE), 4)
```

## 2. Interactive plot map

`forplot_map()` georeferences each tree from its subplot and local `X`/`Y`
coordinates, given the four plot corners. The corners below are approximate
and only for illustration.

```{r map, eval = has_pandoc}
corners <- data.frame(
  Latitude  = c(-19.9000, -19.9009, -19.9000, -19.9009),
  Longitude = c(-40.5500, -40.5500, -40.5490, -40.5490)
)

html <- forplot_map(
  fp,
  vertex_coords = corners,
  voucher_imgs = img_dir,
  dir = out,
  verbose = FALSE
)
basename(html)
```

The resulting self-contained HTML file can be opened in any browser and
shared with the field team; it does not need R or an internet connection,
apart from the background map tiles.

## 3. Collection balance

`forplot_balance()` summarizes how complete the voucher collection is. Here we
skip the HTML and PDF reports (which require pandoc and LaTeX) and keep the
Excel summary:

```{r balance}
bal <- forplot_balance(
  fp,
  plot_size = 1,
  subplot_size = 10,
  render_html = FALSE,
  render_pdf = FALSE,
  dir = out,
  verbose = FALSE
)

sheets <- openxlsx::getSheetNames(bal$xlsx_report)
sheets
summary_tab <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(bal$xlsx_report, sheet = 1)
head(summary_tab)
```

With `render_html = TRUE` the same call produces a navigable report with
whole-plot and per-subplot maps of collected, uncollected and palm
individuals, and a checklist of priority species still lacking vouchers.

## 4. Herbarium label spreadsheet

`forplot_sheets()` fills an empty herbarium template with taxonomy, locality,
collector and standardized notes for every collected tree. The JABOT template
only needs its column names:

```{r template}
jabot_cols <- c("family", "genus", "sp1", "number", "collector", "addcoll",
                "colldd", "collmm", "collyy", "country", "majorarea",
                "minorarea", "uc", "projeto", "locnotes", "latitude",
                "longitude", "altprof", "notes")
template <- as.data.frame(matrix(character(0), ncol = length(jabot_cols),
                                 dimnames = list(NULL, jabot_cols)))
herb <- file.path(out, "jabot_template.xlsx")
openxlsx::write.xlsx(template, herb)
```

By default the function checks that the coordinates fall within `majorarea`
(GADM boundaries) and extracts the altitude from WorldClim; both need an
internet connection. Here we supply `alt` and skip the locality check:

```{r sheets}
labels <- forplot_sheets(
  fp_file_path = fp,
  herb_file_path = herb,
  input_type = "forestplots",
  language = "en",
  majorarea = "ES",
  minorarea = "Santa Teresa",
  protectedarea = "REBIO Augusto Ruschi",
  collector = "G. C. Ottino",
  lat = -19.9,
  long = -40.55,
  alt = 800,
  validate_locality = FALSE,
  dir = out
)

nrow(labels)
head(labels[, c("family", "genus", "sp1", "number")])
labels$notes[1]
```

RAINFOR field codes (tree condition, light exposure) are translated into
plain text and merged with the free-text census notes. Setting
`language = "pt"` or `"es"` writes the notes in Portuguese or Spanish.

## MONITORA data

The same functions read MONITORA spreadsheets with
`input_type = "monitora"`. The bundled `TUM` dataset has three stations; pass
`station_name` to select one:

```{r monitora}
table(TUM$Nome_estacao)

fm <- file.path(out, "TUM.xlsx")
openxlsx::write.xlsx(TUM, fm)

tum_labels <- forplot_sheets(
  fp_file_path = fm,
  herb_file_path = herb,
  input_type = "monitora",
  station_name = "EA-1",
  majorarea = "AP",
  minorarea = "Laranjal do Jari",
  lat = 1.5,
  long = -52.5,
  alt = 300,
  validate_locality = FALSE,
  dir = out
)
nrow(tum_labels)
```

## Herbarium cross-check

`forplot_crossdet()` compares field determinations with the current
determinations of the same vouchers in a JABOT herbarium. It downloads the
herbarium's Darwin Core Archive on the first call (cached afterwards), so it
is not run here:

```{r crossdet, eval = FALSE}
check <- forplot_crossdet(fp, herbaria = "RB", collector_fallback = "G. C. Ottino")
head(check$matches)
```
